newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam flies ailing president out of country.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam flies ailing president out of country.

text.p: Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh has been removed from the Hanoi 108 Army Hospital, where he had been in a critical condition, and flown out of the country, political sources said on Wednesday.
One of the sources said the 75-year-old general, one of the communist country's leadership troika, had been flown to Singapore on Tuesday and admitted to a hospital there.
"He's not in Hospital 108 any more," one source said. "They took him on a special plane and took him out of the country."
The foreign ministry, asked about reports that Anh was in a critical condition after suffering a stroke about 12 days ago, had said on Tuesday that his health was improving.
"According to information we have just received, President Le Duc Anh is in the process of health recovery," the ministry said in a one-sentence statement.

Anh, who holds a key position of influence over the military and security apparatus, is part of a septuagenarian triumvirate which includes Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi and reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet.
According to the constitution, the vice president must stand in if the president is incapacitated for a long period.

Anh's deputy, Nguyen Thi Binh, is not a member of the Politburo or the party's Central Committee. If Anh dies, she would be expected to play only a figurehead role until a successor is chosen and then put to the National Assembly for approval.
Analysts say Anh's departure could reopen an internal debate over leadership succession that had simmered ahead of a key Communist Party congress earlier this year.

Muoi, Anh and Kiet represent a balance of different political hues within the party and come from the north, the centre and the south of the country. Political analysts say Anh is considered to be the most conservative of the three.
